characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: MIRA-3 LMH FE-SEM; metallographic specimens polished (PG-1A) and etched in 10 % nitric acid alcohol
characterization_methods.key_findings: QA-740 SEM shows lath martensite with reverted austenite (A) arrowed between the laths; unlike QA-620 no carbides were observed; fracture surface of QA-740 shows cleavage/quasi-cleavage and dimples crisscrossing without sensible borders, with larger dimples and second cracks
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: secondary-electron imaging; QA-740 micrograph at 5 µm scale bar
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe the micro-laminated δ-ferrite/tempered martensite structure, reverted austenite among laths and tensile fracture morphology

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: EBSD probe (Oxford Instruments) on the FE-SEM; specimens electrochemically polished (10 % perchloric acid + 5 % glycerol + 85 % ethyl alcohol, 15–20 V, 0.8–1.2 A); step size 150 nm; HKL Channel5 software and Python used for analysis
characterization_methods.key_findings: QA-740 shows extensive widely distributed austenite in tempered martensite with elongated ferrite bands visible; GND density BCC 4.84, FCC 2.79 ×10^14 m^-2; EBSD austenite fraction ~50 %; austenitic grain size mostly <1.6–2.0 µm (<4.8 µm for ~90 %)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: BC maps, KAM maps, grain-boundary distribution maps; 50 µm scale bars; austenite highlighted in red
characterization_methods.purpose: Quantify austenite distribution/volume fraction, GND density (BCC/FCC), boundary densities and austenitic grain size statistics

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: SmartLab diffractometer, Cu-Kα radiation at 40 kV and 150 mA; scanning step size 0.02° and scanning speed 2°/min; FullProf software for Rietveld refinement
characterization_methods.key_findings: XRD austenite volume fraction of QA-740 ~51 %; SFE ~33.29 mJ m^-2 (TWIP window 20–40 mJ m^-2); austenite fraction decreased after tensile testing (TRIP)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: specimens 10 × 10 mm before tensile tests and 5 × 20 mm after tensile tests; electrochemically polished as for EBSD
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure austenite content (before/after tensile) and estimate stacking fault energy (SFE) via Rietveld refinement

characterization_methods.key_findings: QA-740: YS 498 ± 3 MPa, TS 725 ± 9 MPa, TE 62.4 ± 4.2 %, yield-tensile ratio 0.69, PSE 45.2 ± 3.7 GPa %
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; strain rate 0.375 min^-1; rod-shaped M10*60 mm specimens, gauge length 25 mm; tensile axis parallel to rolling direction
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure yield strength, tensile strength, total elongation and derive PSE, yield-tensile ratio and work hardening rate

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Calculated equilibrium phase fractions and ferrite/austenite composition partitioning vs temperature (~500–1600 °C) for the Fe–9Mn–5Al-0.3C steel
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: The calculated dual-phase (δ-ferrite + austenite) window and A1/cementite precipitation point (~617 °C) justified the chosen quenching (1050 °C) and intercritical annealing temperatures (620/680/740/800 °C); the 740 °C condition belongs to this selected annealing window

analytical_models.model_note: Geometric-mean definition of average local misorientation at pixel point i

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: KAM maps used to compute average local misorientation; GND density computed for BCC and FCC phases of each condition including QA-740
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: Burger's vector b = 2.887 Å for BCC, 2.563 Å for FCC (measured by XRD); EBSD step size μ = 150 nm
computational_details.simulation_method: GND density calculation from EBSD KAM data

analytical_models.model_note: QA-740 estimated SFE ~33.29 mJ·m^-2, within the 20–40 mJ·m^-2 TWIP window

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Applied to austenite of QA specimens before tensile testing
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: Equation (3) with Zener elastic anisotropy A, shear modulus G_<111>, lattice constant a0, root-mean-square microstrain ε²₅₀ and stacking fault probability SFP
computational_details.simulation_method: Stacking fault energy estimation from XRD parameters
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Estimated SFEs of QA specimens all fall between 20 and 40 mJ m^-2, indicating the TWIP effect is expected during deformation; SFE also correlates inversely with the austenite stability constant k

analytical_models.model_note: QA-740 has the highest k apart from QA-800 (~1.50), i.e. low austenitic stability and notable TRIP effect

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: V_o and V_ε are austenite volume fractions before and after tensile tests, ε the corresponding true strain after tensile test
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: k values (QA-740 ~1.47) trend inversely with SFE, confirming that higher k corresponds to lower austenitic stability and more pronounced TRIP effect

defect_interactions.interaction_type: second crack formation at δ/(γ,α) interfaces
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Ductile deformation accumulates dislocations at the interfaces of δ-ferrite band and tempered martensite lamellar; hardness difference causes stress concentration, initiating cracks. Once formed, cracks are captured by δ-ferrite and propagate into/along the δ-ferrite band forming second cracks like deep valleys (observed in the QA-740 fracture, Fig. 6c).

interfaces.interface_notes: The coarse δ-ferrite grains have deficient high-angle grain boundaries, so microcracks propagate as cleavage within δ-ferrite; the soft δ-ferrite can blunt propagating cracks, giving high cracking resistance.
interfaces.phase_evolution: During annealing at 740 °C reverted austenite nucleated and grew at martensite lath gaps with diffusion of C and Mn into austenite and Al into martensite/ferrite; block boundaries were gradually replaced by AG boundaries as annealing temperature increased. No carbides precipitated at 740 °C and no new martensite formed on air cooling (unlike QA-800).
interfaces.slip_behavior: Dislocation gliding initiates sequentially in ferrite and austenite (soft phases) then tempered martensite; strain-induced martensite acts as obstacle to dislocation glide and site of dislocation accumulation. Work hardening of QA-740 is governed by the three-stage WHR behaviour with TRIP dominating stage III.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: highest product of strength and elongation (PSE) and maximum uniform elongation among HR, IQ-1050 and QA-620/680/740/800

performance.performance_notes: QA-740 had the highest PSE ~45.2 GPa % and the maximum uniform elongation ~62.4 % of all treatment states. More than half of the austenite in QA-740 participated in the TRIP effect, causing the best total elongation. QA-740 showed the highest k value (~1.47, high TRIP activity, lower austenitic stability) together with QA-800. All QA specimens exhibited low yield-to-tensile ratio and could substitute for TRIP 580T/400Y (or 590T/400Y) high strength automobile plates per SAE J2745-2007.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Ingot heated to 1100 °C for 2 h prior to forging (common upstream step of the route that produced QA-740).
Forged into a square forging ingot measuring 80 mm × 70 mm.
Forging ingot reheated to 1100 °C and held for 2 h before hot rolling.
Hot rolled from 80 to 12 mm thickness in eight passes, initial rolling temperature ~1050 °C and finishing rolling temperature ~950 °C (step preceding the QA-740 anneal).
processing_steps.reduction_ratio: from 80 to 12 mm thickness in eight passes
processing_steps.temperature: initial rolling temperature approximately 1050 °C; finishing rolling temperature approximately 950 °C

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Hot-rolled plate air cooled to room temperature, corresponding sample labeled HR; this HR plate is the parent of the IQ-1050 and QA series.

processing_steps.method: intercritical reheating (austenitization in ferrite+austenite dual-phase region)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Hot-rolled plate reheated to 1050 °C (ferrite + austenite dual-phase region) for 1 h.
Water quenching after the 1050 °C/1 h hold, sample labeled IQ-1050; this is the parent process of proc_qa-740.
Water-quenched plate annealed for 1 h at 740 °C, corresponding sample labeled QA-740 (this is the specified sample).
Annealed specimen air cooled to room temperature (per Fig. 1 route, the anneal plateau is closed by air cooling to room temperature).

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: rod-shaped sample size M10*60 mm with gauge length of 25 mm; tensile axis parallel to the rolling direction of the hot-rolled plate
measurement_conditions.test_standard: SAE J2745-2007 (referenced as substitution target TRIP 590T/400Y / TRIP 580T/400Y)

elongation.note: total elongation (TE); also reported as the maximum uniform elongation ~62.4 %

strain_hardening_rate.description: WHR curve of QA-740: three-stage behaviour; red WHR curve decays steeply and plateaus near/below 1100 MPa with a slight upturn towards the end of stage III; necking point at the largest strain of the four QA panels (between 0.4 and 0.5 true strain), fracture close to 0.5 true strain

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: values derived from XRD Rietveld refinement / EBSD before or after tensile testing

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: Austenite grain size distribution: quantity of austenite grains increases as grain size decreases; ~90 % of grains are less than 4.8 μm; the largest bin is <1.6 μm (at/just above 30 % proportion) with 1.6–2.0 μm at about 20 %

phases_present.morphology: fine grains widely distributed among tempered martensitic laths

defects.dislocation_density: BCC 4.84 ×10^14 m^-2 (BCC value reported for the specimen)

phases_present.morphology: elongated band, coarse grains; band remains clearly visible after annealing

structures.overall_structure: Micro-laminated (banded) microstructure consisting of δ-ferrite band and tempered martensite lamellar; after annealing a large number of fine austenite (retained + reverted) grains widely distributed within the tempered martensite region.
Austenite volume fraction of QA-740 determined by EBSD and XRD (the highest among the QA series together with QA-800).

defects.lattice_distortion: KAM map of QA-740 dark blue overall with faint slightly brighter patches, i.e. very low residual misorientation

grain_structure.texture: Grain-boundary map of QA-740 sparser network consisting mostly of red (block) lines with scattered cyan/green, large white areas; AG boundary density peaks just under 1.6 μm^-1 at QA-740 in the QA series

structures.overall_structure: Recovered microstructure with low residual misorientation and sparse grain-boundary network after annealing at 740 °C; AG (austenitic grain) boundary density highest in the QA series.

unmapped_findings: QA-740 austenite stability constant k ~1.47 (highest two values with QA-800 ~1.50) gives the most notable TRIP effect; more than half of the austenite in QA-740 participated in the TRIP effect. (b0066, b0071)

QA-740 SFE ~33.29 mJ·m^-2 lies within the 20–40 mJ·m^-2 TWIP window, so the TWIP effect is expected in addition to TRIP during deformation; the SFE of QA-740 (33.29) is lower than QA-680 (38.27) and higher than QA-800 (31.53). (b0063, b0070)

QA-740 exhibited the largest necking strain among the four QA specimens (necking point between 0.4 and 0.5 true strain, fracture close to 0.5 true strain), and except for QA-680 all QA specimens experienced complete uniform deformation. (figure_010, b0077)

The austenitic grain size distribution of QA specimens (from EBSD, before tensile tests) is similar for all four conditions, with ~90 % of austenite grains smaller than 4.8 μm and the <1.6 μm bin the largest (at/just above 30 % proportion). (b0074, figure_011)
δ-ferrite band remains clearly visible in QA-740 with extensive widely distributed austenite within the tempered martensite. (figure_004)
Second cracks were observed in the fracture of QA-740 (Fig. 6c, two white-arrowed second cracks) due to stress concentration at δ and γ/α interfaces. (b0041, figure_006)
